title: South Texas to get $22B power project tied to data center
key_facts: The US and South Korean governments are working on a plan to bring a large gas power plant to La Salle County, Texas, to power data centres directly.
The US Department of Commerce says the 6.47 gigawatt combined-cycle gas power plant will be built in Encinal, Texas, and operated by Related Companies and NextEra Energy Resources.
The first stage is expected online in 2029 and full capacity in 2032.
Related Digital says the plant will power a 5 GW data centre on an adjacent site, with the remaining power going to the Texas grid.

Related's project page says the data centre would use a closed-loop water cooling system using about the same water daily as an office building; the power project is looking at produced water (a by-product of oil and gas extraction) for cooling.
NextEra says construction would bring 8,400 jobs; the completed power campus is expected to have 170 permanent jobs and the data centre 'hundreds' of permanent jobs.
The project is part of the implementation of the Korea-US trade deal announced on 30 July 2025 and a Strategic Investment MOU signed on 14 Nov 2025.
The article's information comes from releases by NextEra Energy, the US Department of Commerce and Related Digital; the '$22B' figure in the pool headline does not appear in the text read.
quote_evidence: "Project Star demonstrates how energy infrastructure and economic growth can advance together," said John Ketchum, chairman and CEO of NextEra Energy.
The Source: Information in this article comes from a release from NextEra Energy, the U.S. Dept. of Commerce and Related Digital.
The United States and South Korean governments are working together on a plan that would bring a large gas power plant to La Salle County, Texas, to directly power data centers.
why_it_matters_hint: A large gas power plant planned in South Texas to supply a data centre and the state grid; the jobs and water claims come from the project side.
